sections.heading: Section 1: Standard Equation and Features of Circles

questions.q: Find the center and radius of the circle $(x - 3)^2 + (y + 5)^2 = 49$.
questions.answer: Standard form is $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$. Here $h = 3, k = -5, r = \sqrt{49} = 7$.

questions.q: Convert the general equation $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 8y - 11 = 0$ to standard form by completing the square.
Find the equation of the circle passing through the origin with center $(-2, 3)$.

sections.heading: Section 2: Parabolas with Vertical Axis of Symmetry

questions.q: Find the focus and directrix of the parabola $x^2 = 12y$.
questions.answer: $x^2 = 4py \Rightarrow 4p = 12 \Rightarrow p = 3$. Vertical axis, opens up: Focus is $(0, p) = (0, 3)$, directrix is $y = -p = -3$.

questions.q: Find the standard equation of the parabola with vertex $(0, 0)$ and focus $(0, -2)$.
Find the focal diameter (latus rectum length) of $(x - 1)^2 = -16(y + 2)$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Parabolas with Horizontal Axis of Symmetry

questions.q: Find the vertex, focus, and directrix of $(y - 2)^2 = 8(x + 1)$.
questions.answer: $4p = 8 \Rightarrow p = 2$. Vertex is $(h, k) = (-1, 2)$. Opens right: Focus is $(h+p, k) = (1, 2)$, directrix is $x = h - p = -1 - 2 = -3$.

questions.q: Find the equation of a parabola with vertex $(3, -1)$ and focus $(1, -1)$.
questions.answer: Horizontal axis $y = -1$. Opens left because focus $x = 1$ is to the left of vertex $x = 3$. $p = 1 - 3 = -2$. $(y + 1)^2 = 4(-2)(x - 3) = -8(x - 3)$.

questions.q: A satellite dish has the shape of a paraboloid. If the cross-section is $x^2 = 20y$ (in inches), where should the receiver be placed?
choices: At $(0, 5)$, which is $5\text{ inches}$ above the vertex
questions.answer: Signals parallel to the axis reflect to the focus. $4p = 20 \Rightarrow p = 5\text{ inches}$ above the vertex.

questions.q: A suspension bridge cable hangs in the shape of a parabola with towers $100\text{ m}$ apart and $20\text{ m}$ high, touching the road at the center. Find its equation with origin at the vertex.
Why do parabolic headlights use a light source placed exactly at the focus?
choices: Light rays reflecting off the parabolic surface emerge in a parallel beam
It spreads the light in all directions equally
It prevents the mirror from tarnishing
questions.answer: By the geometric reflective property of parabolas, all rays emanating from the focus reflect parallel to the axis of symmetry.
